title: EC-Council CND
summary: EC-Council CND is a professional certification offered by EC-Council. This independent study guide covers all 20 course modules: Network Attacks and Defense Strategies, Administrative Network Security, Technical Network Security, Network Perimeter Security, Endpoint Security - Windows Systems, Endpoint Security - Linux Systems, Endpoint Security - Mobile Devices, Endpoint Security - IoT Devices, Administrative Application Security, Data Security, Enterprise Virtual Network Security, Enterprise Cloud Security, Enterprise Wireless Network Security, Network Traffic Monitoring and Analysis, Network Logs Monitoring and Analysis, Incident Response and Forensics Investigation, Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery, Risk Anticipation with Risk Management, Threat Assessment with Attack Surface Analysis, Threat Prediction with Cyber Threat Intelligence. Every module has a MEDIUM and a HARD scenario exam, written as realistic workplace situations rather than recall questions, so you practise applying each module the way the job asks for it.
objectives: Threat Assessment with Attack Surface Analysis
Threat Prediction with Cyber Threat Intelligence
attributionNote: EC-Council certification content is an independent study guide written for Cyber Pulse Academy and is not affiliated with or endorsed by EC-Council.

beginner.definition: The Certified Network Defender is a security certificate from EC-Council. It is about defending a network instead of breaking into one. Network means the cables, switches, routers and wireless links that carry data between computers. You learn how to protect that path from attackers.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most attacks reach a victim over a network. Employers need people who can watch and protect that path. This certificate shows that you understand both the attack and the defence. It is a natural next step for a network administrator who wants to move into security. It also prepares you for the more advanced defensive and investigative certifications.
howItWorks: Learn the fundamentals first, such as how data moves through the layers of a network.
Study the common network attacks, including denial of service, address spoofing and attacks on wireless links.
Practise with the defensive devices you will meet at work. These include firewalls and intrusion detection systems.
Learn how to write a security policy and how to harden a device against attack.
Train on monitoring and incident response, because a defender must notice and contain an attack quickly.
The exam is multiple choice with scenario questions. Practise choosing the best response to a described event.
beginner.example: Imagine a staff laptop that suddenly sends large amounts of data to an unknown address overseas. A network defender does not simply unplug the laptop and move on. You check the firewall and intrusion detection logs. You look at the domain name server queries and confirm whether the traffic is encrypted. Then you work out whether other machines talk to the same address. Then you isolate the host and start the response process. This exam tests that whole chain of thought.
takeaways: Know your network first. You cannot defend traffic flows you do not understand.
Learn the defensive controls and the attacks together, because exam scenarios mix them.
The weight sits on controls, policies and monitoring. Do not spend all your time on attack theory.
